entries.title: TileForge now blocks packs from uncommitted or unpushed code and publishes successful ZIPs as GitHub releases
entries.detail: The headless CLI (the supported publisher) refuses zip builds when the tree is dirty — full porcelain per the ruled letter, untracked files included; an uncommitted in-tree draft's tracked-only softening was tightened to match §4.1 — or when HEAD is absent from the remote, naming the failed check (exit 3; --no-zip validation stays ungated). Manifests now carry exporter-written contentHashes (SHA-256 of every sibling entry, 173 in the proof pack) beside the standard sourceCommit; in-app exports ship null provenance and cannot pass §5 intake. --release uploads the zip as an immutable GitHub release tagged <zipname>@<commit>, notes carrying sourceCommit + zip SHA-256, existing tag = refuse. Exercised for real at tileforge e3353ec: dirty-tree refusal on a genuinely dirty 29-path tree, unpushed-HEAD refusal, untracked --project refusal, and a clean-worktree PASS build whose manifest hashes all verified via an independent zip reader. No delivery claimed: the release step is code-complete but unexercised (gh keyring auth and the immutable-tag probe are green; the registry stays empty until the next real pack cut) and existing exports/ packs are grandfathered — WorldForge's pinned a5baf52 unaffected. Live friction, by design: the designer's parked scratch (baseline ' - Copy' PNGs, refroads-new/) now blocks main-tree pack builds until their delete/keep call — the clean-worktree escape is documented in --help.

entries.title: World Filler now blocks packs from uncommitted or unpushed code and publishes successful ZIPs as GitHub releases
entries.detail: The exporter (wf-fill export) is now a publishing act per the ruled letter: it refuses when the tree is dirty (git status --porcelain non-empty) or HEAD is on no remote branch (git branch -r --contains HEAD empty), naming the failed check before any work; the dirty-tree refusal was exercised for real on a genuinely dirty 19-path tree (exit 1, nothing written). entries.title: Cliff diagnosis done: the roads-climb-cliffs bug is WorldForge's street carver, and TileForge is missing nothing
entries.detail: Answers to sl-0028, all measured on the b70 pack, no fixes applied yet. (1) PROVENANCE: high-cliff walkability is WorldForge-side semantics, not TileForge tile properties - terrain.rock sits in the loader's BLOCKED_MATERIALS list, and the cliff terraces are adapter-side ART drawn inside the rock mass under an explicit invariant ('every walkable cell stays level 0 - a cliff can never cross traversal'). The assertion the designer remembers giving is the narrower 2026-07-28 moss ruling: bare moss carpet on LEVEL-0 apron rock walks; terraces stay solid. Measured b70 grid: plateau tops 1705 cells with only 79 walkable (every one a road/lane cell), cliff edges 231 with 29 walkable (lane crossings), apron 781 with 157 walkable (moss + graded trails), and the RAMP layer is ALL ZEROS - ramps are never placed by anything, though the package ships four walkable ramp families. The stated intent (edges unwalkable / tops walkable / ramps the access) is NOT implemented: tops are blocked and ramps do not exist. Making tops walkable is a walkability-CONTRACT change touching pack, game, and world_filler - designer-ruled arc, not a quiet fix. Related: world_filler's 'walkable cliff-top tiles' observation (sl-0026) is actually moss carpets and graded/lane cells, not tops. (2) ROADS x CLIFFS: wilderness trails GRADE rock crossings to gravel (zero violations measured), but the city street-web carvers write lanes with NO rock grading - the b70 snowline city carved 108 walkable lane cells at terrace level >= 1 (x 200-237, y 25-26): streets climbing cliff faces with no ramps. That is the designer's road issue. A second ungraded writer (the landmark approach carver) is latent. (3) VERDICT: fixes are ALL WorldForge-lane (grade rock under city-lane and approach carvers, restoring the no-cliff-crossing invariant); the TileForge ask is a NO-OP - current exports still ship road/ruinedroad (legacy per the ROAD-LAYER RETIREMENT ae1eecb+c92d36f, 'roadTypesLegacy shipped, count unchanged'), dirtpath, packedroad, and all four ramp families, byte-identical to the pinned dusk manifest. FORWARD GUARD for TileForge instead: never stop exporting road/ruinedroad/ramp families (city lanes ride the legacy road band; a future walkable-tops arc needs the ramps). Drift note: TileForge's handoff still says WorldForge pins a5baf52 - stale, WF pins ae1eecb since 2026-07-28. RECOMMENDATION: hold the b70 game intake; b71 re-exports after the carver grading fix (small, in-lane); the tops+ramps redesign awaits a designer ruling. || CORRECTION (same session, designer redirect): the TileForge missing-inventory half is SUPERSEDED - restoration was ruled separately (sl-0029); for the record the measurement stands (current TF exports byte-identical to pinned for road families, ATLAS KEPT per ae1eecb). entries.title: Planning asks the game to make the aim crosshair readable — the hardware cursor never scales with the viewport (designer's standing complaint)
entries.detail: Designer flag raised at the evening seam, standing 'forever': the aim crosshair is really hard to see. Planning grounding before the ask: game/main.gd:876 sets uikit cursor_crosshair.png (11x11 per the docs/13 spec row, hotspot 5,5) via Input.set_custom_mouse_cursor — a HARDWARE cursor, drawn at native pixel size in window space, so it never inherits viewport scaling: every sprite scales up on screen while the crosshair stays an ~11-physical-pixel speck, worse at higher display resolutions. This is a readability defect against the kit's own intent (docs/13: 'light core + 1 px dark rim so it survives every floor'), not taste drift. Requirement, not implementation: the crosshair must read at a glance at real gameplay scale, against every palette including dusk, windowed and fullscreen. Recommended lean: fix at the load site in code — scale the cursor texture nearest-neighbor by the actual window content scale (hotspot scaled to match, re-applied if the window scale changes); do NOT hand-edit the uikit pack assets (manifest-hashed — art/contrast changes that sizing cannot fix are an upstream kit cut, recorded as their own ask). Render-only: zero aim-mechanics or hurtbox change. Boot it for the designer and let them taste-rule final size/contrast on screen (a taste ruling is fine post-shift; no feel verdicts tonight). Log completion hands-free referencing this ask; planning sweeps.
